top3.headline: Nvidia's board and Jensen Huang both go public on the affair
top3.whyItMatters: The key AI chip supplier's leadership risk is now on the record for customers and regulators.

top3.headline: Grok Bot team says it shipped 11,000 PRs last month
top3.whyItMatters: Agent-heavy teams claim huge output; ask how quality holds before matching their pace.

top3.headline: Nancy Pelosi's replacement arrives ready to regulate AI
top3.whyItMatters: Congress may get a new AI rules champion; plan compliance before bills land.

items.title: Grok Bot team says it shipped 11,000 PRs last month
items.takeaway: poteto will explain at AI Engineer on Wednesday how the team kept code quality at that volume.
items.soWhat: Agent-scale output is now a team claim; ask what review system keeps that quality real.

items.title: Nancy Pelosi's replacement is ready to regulate AI
items.takeaway: MIT Technology Review reports that Nancy Pelosi's replacement is ready to regulate AI.
items.soWhat: Post-midterm Congress may push AI rules harder; plan compliance before bills arrive.

items.title: Srinivas says Perplexity Teammates usage rises every day
items.takeaway: He says weekend usage held and Teammates for financial research ship this week. No absolute numbers.
items.soWhat: Workplace agents are expanding into finance research; ask for base numbers before trusting growth claims.

items.title: Trump's 60 Minutes interview turns to AI safety
items.takeaway: The Verge reports the interview touched on AI safety and a threat to arrest an AI executive.
items.soWhat: AI leaders now face political risk at the very top, not only regulatory risk.

items.title: Nathan Benaich: defenders need open cyber models too
items.takeaway: He says Hugging Face found API guardrails slowed an intrusion probe and used a self-hosted open model.
items.soWhat: Closed-model guardrails can block your own security team; keep an open-model option for incidents.

items.title: Disney and Adobe are building generative AI tools together
items.takeaway: The Verge reports a partnership on generative AI tools between the two companies.
items.soWhat: Major rights holders are choosing licensed creative AI partners over fighting the tools.

items.title: Lenny's How I AI: a founder builds a better Duolingo with Codex
items.takeaway: William Imoh walks through how he built a better Duolingo with Codex.
items.soWhat: Single founders are shipping consumer products with coding agents; watch the build-versus-buy math.

items.title: 'Software factory' is a buzzword for a real shift, builders say
items.takeaway: Pocock calls the term hype bait but says it names a real change from this year. Garry Tan says you will want your own software factory.
items.soWhat: Ignore the label and ask how many agent-run pipelines your engineering team actually operates.

related.name: Garry Tan: you'll want your own software factory
Garry Tan on Apple and software factories

items.title: Meng To rebuilds his apartment as a walkable 3D web scene
items.takeaway: Built with Opus 5.5 in three.js for tutorial videos: walkable in the browser, adjustable lighting, render styles, every object defined in code.
items.soWhat: Designers can now build interactive 3D spaces from prompts, without a 3D modeling team.

items.title: MIT Tech Review: the climate case for AI has not been made
items.takeaway: MIT Technology Review argues the climate case for AI is unmade. A Nov 4 piece says Texas's data center boom might be kaput.
items.soWhat: Expect sustainability questions on every AI infrastructure plan your board signs off.

related.name: MIT TR: Texas data center buildout might be kaput

items.title: Simon Willison hides AI-written PR descriptions behind a fold
items.takeaway: He wraps most of each AI-generated GitHub PR description in a collapsed details tag, which GitHub Markdown supports.
items.soWhat: Small formatting rules can keep reviewers from drowning in AI-generated text.

related.name: Simon Willison: hide slop PR descriptions behind details

items.title: Lyn Alden: Japan's real market force is its overseas cash
items.takeaway: Alden says Japan's quiet Godzilla is not the carry trade but its net international investment position, from pensions to private investors.
items.soWhat: Watch Japan's pension and private money abroad, not just the carry trade, for global market risk.

items.title: Theo ran up to 25 Opus threads on under 20% of plan
items.takeaway: Theo says 8 to 25 Opus 5.5 threads ran most of the day on under 20% of a $200 Claude plan, while parallel reviews hammer his Codex plans.
items.soWhat: Heavy parallel agent work can fit in flat-fee plans, so measure usage before buying API capacity.

items.title: Garry Tan's evals say the Jev agent-cost article replicates
items.takeaway: His gstack-evals project re-ran the article on cutting agent bills by 90% with Jev Engineering and Kimi K3, and reports it replicates.
items.soWhat: Agent cost claims are getting independent checks; ask vendors for the same before you switch.

related.name: Article: cut your agent bill by 90% with Jev Engineering

items.title: Theo: coding models still botch MCP authentication for agents
items.takeaway: Theo says Opus makes bad assumptions setting up MCP auth and builds something that fails. He is writing his own MCP guide for his agents.
items.soWhat: Have a human review any agent-built MCP auth before it touches production systems.

related.name: Theo: LLMs are still bad at building tools for agents

items.title: Lyn Alden: one-person risk undercuts a mega cap's value
items.takeaway: Alden says investors pay a premium expecting mega caps not to hinge on one person. Either tech and scale are the moat, or it is flimsy.
items.soWhat: Boards should test whether their moat survives without the person at the top.

items.title: Nvidia board opens independent probe into Jensen Huang
items.takeaway: Independent directors and outside counsel will review Huang's tie to a Megaspeed executive. Nvidia has now posted a board statement and a staff letter from Huang.
items.soWhat: The leading AI chip supplier now carries key-person and export-control risk at once.

related.name: The Verge: full text of Jensen Huang's memo to Nvidia

items.title: Cursor's poteto shares skills that map an app's state machines
items.takeaway: In pstack, /create-formal-verification-skill models state machines per subsystem and /statechart visualizes key user flows.
items.soWhat: Agents can now map the hidden logic in your app before they change it.

items.title: Apple pushes to ship a Siri that acts inside apps
items.takeaway: Per Bloomberg's Gurman, Ternus is pressing Federighi to speed Siri up. First-party app control is expected with iOS 27.3, third-party apps likely in spring.
items.soWhat: If Siri can order and book inside apps, customers may stop opening yours.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin: back ETH as store of value, not fee burner
items.takeaway: He says the fee-burning case was never that strong and optimizing for it would hurt decentralization; store of value aligns with it.
items.soWhat: Protocol founders are choosing decentralization over fee revenue, a design trade any platform faces.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin: a data center slowdown looks net good
items.takeaway: Vitalik argues algorithmic progress lets today's data centers match bigger ones within about four years, buying time to harden against cyber and bio risks.
items.soWhat: Opposition to data centers now has a capability-neutral case that investors and boards will hear.

items.title: Anthropic IPO buyers see valuation as low as $1.1 trillion
items.takeaway: Bloomberg reports IPO valuation expectations for Anthropic are under pressure after the AI market rout. Headline-level only.
items.soWhat: Watch for lab pricing and contract terms to shift as investors push valuations down.

voices.quote: we are entering a renaissance in programming language and runtime research, and a golden age of software testing and verification. it's time to rewrite all software.
I really hope Jensen stays, he is the champion for open source, and if Nvidia is ruled by corpo ladder climbers instead we are in for very dark days ahead
You're really going to want your own software factory
Every gripe you have about bad managers is a bug report for interacting with agents.

hotOnX.text: A golden age of software testing and verification is here. It's time to rewrite all software.
hotOnX.note: Builders debate whether agents plus verification make full rewrites practical.

hotOnX.text: 'Software Factory' is hype and a bandwagon, but it names a real change in how teams work.
hotOnX.note: Engineers are split on whether the label describes real change or marketing.

hotOnX.text: Turned my apartment into a walkable three.js scene with Opus 5.5.
hotOnX.note: Designers see 3D web scenes becoming a prompt-sized job.

hotOnX.text: Talk Wednesday at AI Engineer: how the Grok Bot team shipped 11,000 PRs last month without compromising quality.
hotOnX.note: Teams want the method behind agent-scale output that holds quality.

hotOnX.text: Perplexity Teammates usage has gone up every day since launch, weekend included.
hotOnX.note: Watchers want proof that workplace agents keep usage after launch week.
